humanities_role_explanation: Evaluates models on college-level exam questions in humanities disciplines like Art, Art Theory, Music, History, and Literature, which require discipline-specific knowledge and professional reasoning rather than generic reading comprehension.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Combines text-based multiple-choice options with images (diagrams, art, maps, charts). It also introduces a vision-only setting where the entire question and its choices are embedded inside a single screenshot or photo.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Evaluates academic-grade multiple-choice QA involving factual recall, logical and quantitative calculations, visual reasoning over complex diagrams, causal/temporal analysis of history cartoons, and aesthetic interpretation of art and music notation.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Evaluates broad multimodal reasoning across 30 college-level subjects spanning humanities, social sciences, sciences, and engineering.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source models including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, InternVL2, and LLaVA-OneVision.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses accuracy and Levenshtein-distance-based OCR similarity scores.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint was published in September 2024.

summary: MMMU-Pro is a more robust version of the Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning (MMMU) benchmark, designed to evaluate true multimodal understanding without relying on statistical shortcuts. It accomplishes this by filtering out questions solvable by text-only LLMs, expanding the multiple-choice option pool from 4 to 10 choices, and introducing a vision-only setting where text-based questions are embedded directly into images.
key_findings: Models experience significant performance drops on MMMU-Pro compared to original MMMU, with decreases ranging from 16.8% to 26.9%. GPT-4o is the leading model but drops from 69.1% on MMMU Val to 54.0% on the standard setting and 49.7% on the vision-only setting, leaving a massive gap to human expert performance (~85%). Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting consistently benefits reasoning-intensive subjects, while explicit OCR prompts show minimal overall impact.
facets_explanation: The benchmark questions are sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, representing pre-existing reference material. Correctly answering them requires deep domain-specific knowledge beyond what is visible in the presented diagrams or images. Human experts and model filters were used to resolve ambiguities and eliminate low-quality or poorly aligned questions, treating annotator divergence as noise to be eliminated.
results_explanation: The paper reports that model performance drops significantly on the more difficult MMMU-Pro compared to MMMU (Val), with the largest overall degradation of 26.9 percentage points (rounded to 27) reported for 'VILA-1.5-40B', which falls from '51.9' on 'MMMU (Val)' to an overall average of 25.0% on MMMU-Pro. On the 'Standard (10 Opts)' split, 'Claude 3.5 Sonnet' achieves the highest model accuracy of '55.0%' compared to the 'Human Expert (High)' baseline of '85.4%', resulting in a human-model gap of 30.4 percentage points (rounded to 30). On the 'Vision' split, 'GPT-4o (0513)' is the best performing model with '49.7%' accuracy compared to the 'Human Expert (High)' baseline of '85.4%'.
